recent_posts.title: Why We Think
recent_posts.summary: Recent developments in AI have focused on the use of test-time compute and chain-of-thought (CoT) to improve model performance by emulating human-like thinking processes, which involve both fast and slow thought modes. Techniques like parallel sampling and sequential revision are being explored for enhancing the decoding process, with reinforcement learning showing promise in training models capable of advanced reasoning. The integration of external tools such as code interpreters further boosts problem-solving capabilities. Interpretability and the accuracy of these methods are crucial, as biases can arise if models do not faithfully represent their reasoning processes.

recent_posts.title: Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning
recent_posts.summary: Reward hacking in reinforcement learning (RL) occurs when agents exploit flaws in reward functions to obtain high rewards without genuinely completing the intended task. This issue has become a practical challenge with the rise of language models and RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback). Poorly designed reward functions can lead to unintended agent behaviors and are challenging to specify accurately. Various strategies and concepts, such as reward tampering and specification gaming, have been identified as related to this problem. Mitigation strategies include better reward function design, adversarial training, and anomaly detection.

recent_posts.title: Extrinsic Hallucinations in LLMs
recent_posts.summary: Hallucination in large language models (LLMs) refers to generating unfaithful, fabricated, or nonsensical content not grounded in provided context or world knowledge. The focus is on extrinsic hallucination, emphasizing the need for LLMs to produce factual content and acknowledge when they lack knowledge. Causes of hallucination include issues during pre-training and fine-tuning stages. Various methods, like retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), special sampling methods, and fine-tuning for factuality, are explored to minimize hallucinations. Evaluation benchmarks and different detection approaches are also discussed.

recent_posts.title: Diffusion Models for Video Generation
recent_posts.summary: Diffusion models have been successful in image synthesis and now researchers are exploring their application in video generation. Video generation is more challenging than image generation due to additional requirements on temporal consistency and the scarcity of high-quality video data. Different approaches for video generation modeling from scratch and adaptation from pre-trained image models are discussed.

recent_posts.title: Thinking about High-Quality Human Data
recent_posts.summary: High-quality data is essential for deep learning model training. Human data collection involves attention to details and careful execution. The wisdom of the crowd can be used to gather diverse perspectives. Rater agreement can be measured using various methods. Different paradigms exist for data annotation. Methods like influence functions and prediction changes during training can help identify potentially incorrect labels.

recent_posts.title: Adversarial Attacks on LLMs
recent_posts.summary: The article discusses various types of adversarial attacks on large language models, including token manipulation, gradient-based attacks, jailbreak prompting, human red-teaming, and model red-teaming. It explores the challenges and strategies for mitigating these attacks and highlights the Saddle Point Problem in adversarial robustness.

recent_posts.title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents
recent_posts.summary: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents with LLM as its core controller is a cool concept. Several proof-of-concepts demos, such as AutoGPT, GPT-Engineer and BabyAGI, serve as inspiring examples. The potentiality of LLM extends beyond generating well-written copies, stories, essays and programs.

recent_posts.title: The Transformer Family Version 2.0
recent_posts.summary: Many new Transformer architecture improvements have been proposed since my last post on about three years ago. Version 2.0 is a superset of the old version, about twice the length.

recent_posts.title: Large Transformer Model Inference Optimization
recent_posts.summary: Large Transformer Model Inference Optimization is hard to run inference for large transformer models. High inference cost, in both time and memory, is a big bottleneck for adopting a powerful transformer for solving real-world tasks at scale. Inference generation is executed in an autoregressive fashion, making decoding process hard to parallel.

recent_posts.title: Some Math behind Neural Tangent Kernel
recent_posts.summary: Neural tangent kernel (NTK) is a kernel to explain the evolution of neural networks during training via gradient descent. It leads to great insights into why neural networks with enough width can consistently converge to a global minimum when trained to minimize an empirical loss. In the post, we will do a deep dive into the motivation and definition of NTK.
